sectionsContent.title: Vectors & Vector Basics — Draw & Describe

concept.summary: A vector is a quantity with both magnitude and direction. You draw it as an arrow: the length shows magnitude (to a stated scale), and the angle it points shows direction. Every vector's direction can be written three equivalent ways — a positive course angle (0° to 360°, counted counterclockwise starting from East), that same angle written as a negative number, or a compass phrase like "35° North of East." Given any one of the three, you can always find the other two.
keyIdeas: Course angles start at East (0°) and count counterclockwise — not from North, and not clockwise.
A negative course angle is the same direction as the positive one minus 360°.
A compass phrase can be written two ways for the same vector — 35° North of East is the same direction as 55° East of North, because the two angles always add to 90°.

items: Measuring an angle with a protractor and plotting a point from an x–y coordinate (U0 S0.4).
A scalar is magnitude only; today a vector adds direction to that.
Reading today's reference circle: course angles increase counterclockwise from East.

sectionsContent.title: Vector Addition & Subtraction — Draw & Solve

concept.summary: Adding vectors tip-to-tail means drawing the second vector starting exactly at the tip of the first — the resultant is the single arrow from the start of the first vector to the tip of the last. Subtracting a vector means adding its reverse: flip the vector you're subtracting 180° (same length, opposite direction), then add tip-to-tail exactly like before.
keyIdeas: A − B is the same operation as A + (−B). The only new step is reversing B's direction before you add.
When the two vectors are perpendicular, the resultant's magnitude comes from the Pythagorean theorem and its direction from inverse tangent.
Draw first, calculate second — the sketch tells you whether your numeric answer is a reasonable size and direction.

items: Tip-to-tail construction and the three ways to describe a vector's direction (S2.1).
The Pythagorean theorem and inverse tangent, from your notebook (U0 Math Review).
Displacement as a vector quantity (U1 S1.1).
